content: In Amos, what should roll on like a river?
explanation: And righteousness like a stream. “But let justice roll on like a river, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream.” (Amos 5:24, BSB)

content: In Amos's vision, what was in the Lord's hand by the wall?
explanation: It measured Israel's straightness. ““A plumb line,” I replied.” (Amos 7:8, BSB)

content: In Amos, what was Amos doing when the LORD called him?
explanation: He was a herdsman. “But the LORD took me from following the flock and said to me, ‘Go, prophesy to My people Israel.’” (Amos 7:15, BSB)

content: In Amos, what kind of famine will God send?
explanation: People will search for God's word. “but a famine of hearing the words of the LORD.” (Amos 8:11, BSB)

content: In Amos, from which town was the shepherd-prophet Amos?
explanation: He was among its sheepherders. “These are the words of Amos, who was among the sheepherders of Tekoa” (Amos 1:1, BSB)

content: In Amos, what did Amos say he was before God called him?
explanation: He was not a professional prophet. “rather, I was a herdsman and a tender of sycamore-fig trees.” (Amos 7:14, BSB)

content: In Amos, righteousness should flow like what?
explanation: Justice rolls on like a river. “and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream.” (Amos 5:24, BSB)

content: In Amos, Amos's words came two years before what event?
explanation: In the days of King Uzziah. “what he saw concerning Israel two years before the earthquake” (Amos 1:1, BSB)

content: In Amos, which kind of trees did Amos tend?
explanation: He was a farmer, not a prophet. “I was a herdsman and a tender of sycamore-fig trees.” (Amos 7:14, BSB)
